screening_reason: Crew bugged the wrong approach speed and continued through 500 ft about 17 kt fast to land.
Pilot dived from high on final, sinking 1800 fpm through 500 ft, and continued to land.
Captain broke out high at minimums, steepened below glideslope through pull-up warnings and landed with a tailwind on a wet runway.
Captain continued after sink rate warnings below 500 ft about 8 kt fast and touched down about 2500 ft down the runway.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
screening_reason: Captain overruled the FO's go-around call after a pull-up warning on a high, steep valley approach and continued to land.
Captain insisted on flaps 3 on a short runway and flew a flat, low final, possibly touching down on the displaced threshold.
FO floated and touched down at or beyond the end of the touchdown zone, then hesitated on the captain's go-around call.
Fatigued crew continued from high through a terrain warning, over the speed limit below 500 ft, and landed with flaps 25 instead of 30.
Captain accepted a late runway change from a high base, rushed the approach and continued to land with speed and configuration outside stabilised approach criteria.
Crew on a training flight decelerated too slowly to make the assigned exit, missed it and stayed on the runway, so following traffic had to go around.
Crew misidentified the traffic in a line-up-and-wait-behind-landing-traffic clearance and taxied over the hold line, so the landing aircraft was sent around.
Crew rushed the line-up for an immediate takeoff and set takeoff thrust before the main gear trucks had locked, rejected on the runway, and the aircraft on short final went around.
Crew missed a published no-reverse-turn restriction in planning and made an unauthorised reverse turn off the runway, and an aircraft on final was sent around.
Crew read back a hold-short but treated a later follow-traffic instruction as clearance, crossed the runway and could not clear it, so landing traffic was sent around.
Crew landed short and chose an early exit that led towards a taxiway with departing traffic, were held still on the runway, and the following aircraft went around.
Crew hand-flew a night visual approach and descended below the glidepath to about 2300 ft until a tower low altitude alert.
Crew misidentified a nearby airport at night and descended below the assigned 1600 ft to about 1000 ft before ATC alerted them.
PF relied on speedbrakes without timely flaps and descended about 400 ft below the assigned altitude into a stick shaker before the captain recovered.
After a false localizer capture the hand-flying FO descended to about 1700 ft on a segment charted at 2000 ft until the PM called it and EGPWS sounded.
Task-saturated crew on a charted river visual descended about 1000 ft below the charted altitude without VNAV PATH engaged and went around after a low altitude alert.
Crew cleared for a visual 17 nm out set the 6700 ft FAF altitude and descended from 13000 ft until a terrain warning at about 8000 ft.
While slowing and configuring late the crew did not notice the aircraft descend from the selected 1900 ft to 1600 ft until a GPWS obstacle caution.
PF overrode the autopilot in the turn to final and lost about 200 ft below the 2100 ft set altitude leading to a terrain warning and a go-around.
Crew accepted direct to the FAF on an RNP approach without knowing the chart note or checking the MVA chart and descended below the ATC altitude to about 3100 ft near terrain.
Captain read the wrong fix altitude off the plate and descended on downwind toward 2100 ft instead of 2900 ft until an ATC altitude alert.
Crew chose to fly high on the arrival to avoid wake and crossed BARIN about 900 ft above the 6000 ft restriction.
Rushed into an amended visual approach the PF followed the FMS vertical guidance without confirming its altitudes and descended low enough for an ATC altitude alert.
After an approach clearance to maintain 15000 ft the crew set the FAF altitude and descended to about 11000 ft below the MSA until ATC called it.
Captain set the MCP to touchdown zone believing VNAV was engaged and the aircraft descended in level change about 700 ft below the next target altitude until ATC alerted and the crew went around.
Captain went direct to the FAF and set 2000 ft instead of the published 2900 ft and the PM did not catch it until an ATC altitude alert.

Distracted by fuel planning with holding speed near the low-speed band the crew let the aircraft sink below FL360 after a VNAV descent and drew an RA from traffic at FL350 then hit the stick shaker following it.
PF hand-flew with speedbrakes out after an overspeed and descended about 300 ft below the 6500 ft crossing altitude to 6200 ft (about 1700 ft above ground) until tower called it.

PF descended from 4300 ft over a known ridge against the captain's caution with the autopilot in pitch mode and did not level off until a terrain pull-up warning and the captain took over for a go-around.
On vectors off the approach to burn fuel the crew read back and descended to 10000 ft in what both reporters think was a misheard clearance to 12000 ft until ATC questioned it below the MIA.
FPA was selected to chase a VNAV path shown below them before the fix while the captain stated the 5000 ft restriction and the aircraft descended below 5000 ft until ATC queried it.

After a visual approach clearance the crew set the 2000 ft FAF altitude and descended early without arming the approach until a tower low altitude warning with about 800 ft on the radio altimeter before the fix.
Crew engaged HDG about 35 seconds late for an assigned turn on vectors and did not verify the mode had engaged.
Crew took expect radar vectors to mean after DSNEE and flew on past it on the STAR heading without a vector, leaving the arrival.
Crew read back a present-heading instruction for opposing traffic but kept turning on the SID instead, climbing through the traffic's altitude without seeing it.
Crew flew a left turn on a read-back heading they thought non-standard without querying it, then over-banked to about 45 degrees when ATC ordered an immediate right turn.
Crew let the autopilot overshoot final on a visual approach in a tailwind and the FO over-banked to about 38-40 degrees correcting.
Crew did not notice the SID had dropped from the FMC after a route change and followed an early off-SID turn after takeoff.
Crew misheard and read back direct PALCO instead of FEKKO and flew toward the wrong fix, then got a TCAS RA.
FO chose a green-needle intercept close to the fix, the localizer did not capture and the aircraft flew through final while speed decayed to stick shaker.
Crew departed with the speed selector in manual instead of FMS, so the aircraft failed to accelerate on the SID and ATC turned them off course.
On a STAR the captain rebugged to 300 kt and the first officer descended at 5000 fpm, overspeeding toward 320 kt and then pitching up abruptly at 1.6 g.
After discontinuing an approach the crew climbed in vertical speed with speedbrakes still out, failed to climb as assigned, and later oversped the flaps in a weather go-around.
In turbulence the first officer disconnected the autopilot and pitched up while levelling off on the SID with traffic above and below, triggering the stick shaker.
Given a vector at 2500 ft the captain pressed TOGA instead, then oversped the flaps, reached about 40 degrees of bank and descended to about 1200 ft above ground near conflicting traffic.
Assigned 310 kt or better in descent, the captain pulled back hard with full speedbrake to stop a speed rise, triggering the stick shaker, then slowed below the assigned speed.
